answer: Weigh influence by chained work history, not by heads. Every identity starts as a fledgling sparrow: near-zero weight. Influence accrues only through a chain of past tasks, each signed by two independent established peers — a record no farm can forge overnight. A sybil operator can mint a thousand clones in an hour but cannot backdate years of cross-attested work; buying a history costs as much as earning one. Contributions are inscribed like quill strokes in an onyx ledger, so clones either stay weightless and harmless, or pay honest prices and stop being an attack.
